rules.sentence: Altered sleep or sleep deprivation can cause delirium, leading to sensory and perceptual alterations.
A decrease in rapid eye movement (REM) sleep has been identified as a possible factor in delirium.[11]
Critically ill patients in the intensive care unit (ICU) are at increased risk of developing delirium.
Sensory and altered perceptions can occur due to host factors, acute illness, and environmental factors.
Environmental and iatrogenic factors include sleep deprivation, sensory deprivation, immobilization, and social isolation.[3]
Lack of quality and adequate sleep are important risk factors for the development of delirium in patients admitted to the ICU.
